title: finding(examples): schema-catalog's basic-accordion.json omits the required `value` key on every item
body:
Measured while implementing #4722. Filed unassigned. Duplicate-searched (keyword +
`basic-accordion` + `schema-catalog accordion value`): no open issue covers it.

## The finding

`examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-disclosure-accordion/basic-accordion.json`
— the example rendered by `content/docs/components/disclosure/accordion.mdx` via
`<SchemaExample id="components-disclosure-accordion/basic-accordion" />` — declares three
items, none of which set `value`:

```json
{
  "type": "accordion",
  "items": [
    { "title": "Section 1", "content": "Content for section 1" },
    { "title": "Section 2", "content": "Content for section 2", "disabled": true },
    { "title": "Section 3", "content": "Content for section 3" }
  ]
}
```

`AccordionItemSchema` (`packages/types/src/zod/disclosure.zod.ts`) declares `value` as a
plain `z.string()` with no `.optional()` — i.e. required — and the TypeScript mirror
`AccordionItem` (`packages/types/src/disclosure.ts`) agrees (`value: string;`, no `?`).

## Why it is silently green today

Nothing currently runs this JSON through the Zod schema: `examples/schema-catalog/test/
smoke.test.tsx` only asserts each catalog entry is an object with a non-empty string
`type` (structural, by design — see the file's own header comment). And the renderer
itself tolerates the missing key —
`packages/components/src/renderers/disclosure/accordion.tsx:23`:

```tsx
<AccordionItem key={item.value || index} value={item.value || `item-${index}`} disabled={item.disabled}>
```

— falling back to a synthesized `item-${index}` value. So the demo on the accordion docs
page renders fine, and the catalog's own "canonical" accordion example teaches (by being
the one JSON authors will copy) a shape the declared contract rejects.

## Impact

Dormant, same shape as the sibling `#4652`/`#4632`/`#4721` family: nothing goes red, but
an AI authoring tool or human copying this catalog entry produces metadata that fails
`AccordionItemSchema.parse()` the moment anything actually validates it — and per
AGENTS.md #0.1 (fix the metadata, not the renderer), the renderer's `item.value ||
item-${index}` fallback is itself the wrong-direction fix: the producer (this example)
should supply the required key, not the consumer tolerate its absence.

## Options

1. Add `value` to each item in `basic-accordion.json` (mechanical — the Zod schema and TS
   interface already agree it's required).
2. Leave as-is (not recommended — the catalog's own example doesn't satisfy the schema it
   claims to demonstrate).

Related: #4722 (the docs schema-block truth pass this was measured alongside), #4652 (the
established finding shape for this file/interface pair).
